title: Robust Hate Speech Detection in Social Media: A Cross-Dataset Empirical Evaluation
benchmark_measurement: Detection of hate speech targeted at religious groups as part of a multi-class hate speech classification task.
base_benchmarks: AYR (Are You a Racist or Am I Seeing Things?)
MMHS (Multilingual and Multi-Aspect Hate Speech Analysis)
DEAP (Detecting East Asian Prejudice on Social Media)
LSC (Large Scale Crowdsourcing and Characterization of Twitter Abusive Behavior)
findings: When trained on the unified dataset, transformer-based models achieved moderate performance in detecting religious hate speech, with F1 scores ranging from 40.3 to 52.6. This performance was generally lower than for other hate speech categories like sexism, racism, and disability. The SVM baseline performed very poorly on the religion class with an F1 score of 4.1.
references: Raza Ali, Umar Farooq, Umair Arshad, Waseem Shahzad, and Mirza Omer Beg. 2022. Hate speech detection on twitter using transfer learning. Computer Speech & Language, 74:101365.
